title: 第二十四章 时间跳跃理论的学术研讨会第二十四章 时间跳跃理论的学术研讨会
lines: 第二十四章：时间跳跃理论的学术研讨会
九月的风卷着梧桐叶掠过燕北大学的林荫道，物理学院报告厅外的电子屏正滚动播放着红色宋体字——“第一届时间物理前沿研讨会”。林辰站在厅外的回廊里，指尖无意识地摩挲着公文包上的磨损纹路，包里装着他熬了三个通宵才定稿的论文，标题旁用铅笔标注着一行小字：“关于时间非线性跃迁的数学模型修正”。
“林老师，您也到了？”身后传来轻快的女声，周曼琪抱着一摞装订好的资料快步走来，白大褂袖口沾着点蓝黑墨水，“刚才在后台看到您的名字牌了，居然安排在主会场第一个发言，紧张吗？”
林辰扯了扯领带笑了笑。他认识周曼琪是在去年的量子力学研讨会上，这个刚博士毕业的姑娘总爱抱着笔记本追在各路专家身后问问题，眼睛亮得像淬了光的星星。此刻她胸前的工作牌还别歪了，林辰伸手帮她扶正，金属卡扣碰到指尖时，两人都想起去年在茶水间撞翻咖啡杯的窘迫——当时她手里那篇关于时间悖论的草稿，被褐色液体晕开了好大一片。
报告厅里渐渐坐满了人。前排的银发老者们大多穿着熨帖的西装，手里的会议手册边缘已经被翻得起了毛边；后排的年轻学者们则埋着头在平板电脑上敲敲打打，时不时抬头瞟一眼**台上方的投影幕布。林辰注意到第三排靠窗的位置坐着个穿深灰风衣的男人，侧脸轮廓在阳光下显得格外冷硬，手里转着支黑色钢笔，目光却像钉在他身上似的。
“接下来有请燕北大学物理学院林辰副教授，为我们带来《时间非线性跃迁的数学模型修正》报告。”主持人的声音透过音响传来时，林辰感觉手心沁出了薄汗。他走上**台，调试麦克风的瞬间，瞥见台下那灰风衣男人忽然停下转笔的动作，从公文包里抽出了个巴掌大的银色仪器，屏幕上跳动着淡绿色的波纹。
“传统时间理论认为，时间轴是单向延伸的线性存在……”林辰的声音逐渐平稳下来，激光笔在幕布上划出明亮的光斑，“但根据我在高维空间方程中的推导，当引力场强度达到临界值时，时间可能出现局部折叠——就像把两张叠放的纸戳穿，形成一个连通的孔洞。”
台下响起一阵低低的议论声。周曼琪坐在第一排，手里的钢笔在笔记本上飞快地移动，忽然抬头问道：“林老师，您的模型里提到‘时间坐标的重叠’，这是否意味着在某个特定节点，过去和未来会同时存在？”
“理论上是的。”林辰调出一组三维坐标系，“这里的关键是找到引力场的共振频率，就像找到打开那扇门的钥匙。”
话音刚落，第三排的灰风衣男人忽然站起身。他的声音低沉而清晰，穿透了场内的嘈杂：“林副教授，您是否考虑过这种‘跳跃’的不可逆性？如果某个物体进入了时间孔洞，它还有可能回到原坐标吗？”
林辰皱起眉。这个问题恰好戳中了他模型中最薄弱的环节——他的推导只能证明时间折叠的可能性，却无法计算返程的轨迹。“目前还没有完善的解决方案，”他坦诚道，“但我认为……”
“我认为这根本不可能。”灰风衣男人打断他，缓步走上讲台。他从口袋里掏出一枚银色怀表，表盖打开的瞬间，林辰忽然注意到他左手手腕上有一道淡粉色的疤痕，形状像个扭曲的“s”。“十年前，我也曾提出过类似的理论。”男人的目光扫过台下，“直到我亲眼看到实验对象在强引力场中解体，变成一串无法捕捉的时空碎片。”
报告厅里顿时鸦雀无声。周曼琪惊讶地张大眼睛，手里的钢笔“啪嗒”一声掉在地上。林辰盯着那枚怀表，表针正在逆时针转动，表盘内侧刻着一行模糊的小字：“19:33，永不复返”。
“您是谁？”林辰的声音有些发紧。
男人合上怀表，嘴角勾起一抹复杂的笑意：“我叫陈默，曾经是这里的研究员。”他顿了顿，目光落在林辰的公文包上，“林老师，您论文的第三十七页，是不是少了一组引力常数的修正值？”
林辰猛地愣住。那组数据是他昨天深夜才发现的错误，还没来得及修改——这个叫陈默的男人怎么会知道？
就在这时，报告厅的灯光忽然闪烁了一下。周曼琪弯腰捡钢笔时，无意间看到陈默风衣下摆露出的半截仪器，屏幕上的绿色波纹正和窗外的阳光产生奇异的共振。她忽然想起三天前在档案室看到的旧报纸，头版新闻上的实验室爆炸照片里，有个模糊的身影手腕上也有那样一道疤痕。
“陈先生，”周曼琪站起身，声音带着不易察觉的颤抖，“您说的实验，是不是发生在2013年9月17日的三号实验室？”
陈默的脸色瞬间变得苍白。怀表从他手中滑落，在讲台的木地板上摔成两半，玻璃碎片里映出无数个重叠的影子——有年轻的陈默在实验室里调试仪器，有穿着白大褂的林辰在黑板上推导公式，还有个扎着马尾辫的女孩蹲在地上捡钢笔，和此刻的周曼琪一模一样。
灯光彻底熄灭了。应急灯亮起的瞬间，林辰看到陈默的身影正在变得透明，就像被水浸透的墨痕。“别再找那组数据了，”陈默的声音仿佛从很远的地方传来，“有些门，打开了就再也关不上……”
他的身影彻底消失时，林辰忽然发现自己手里多了半块摔碎的怀表。表盘内侧的字迹变得清晰起来，下面还有一行新刻的小字：“2023年9月17日，燕北大学”。
应急灯熄灭，正常照明重新亮起。台下的学者们还在低声讨论着刚才的争论，仿佛刚才的一切只是幻觉。周曼琪捡起地上的钢笔，发现笔帽上多了一道浅浅的划痕，和她三天前在档案室看到的旧照片里，那支掉在爆炸现场的钢笔一模一样。
林辰握紧了那半块怀表，忽然冲向自己的座位。他翻开公文包，拿出论文的第三十七页——原本空白的修正栏里，不知何时多了一行工整的字迹，笔迹和他自己的几乎一模一样：“引力常数修正值：6.674184x10^-11，此路不通”。
报告厅外的梧桐叶还在往下掉，阳光透过玻璃窗在地板上投下移动的光斑。周曼琪走到林辰身边，看着他指尖的颤抖，忽然轻声道：“您说，刚才那个人……会不会是从十年后回来的？”
林辰没有回答。他看着窗外掠过的一片梧桐叶，恍惚间觉得那叶片的轨迹似乎在哪里见过——或许是在某个被遗忘的公式里，或许是在某段即将到来的时光中。怀表的齿轮还在无声地转动，像是在计数着某个正在逼近的节点。

Chapter 24: Academic seminar on time jump theory
The September wind swept the sycamore leaves across the boulevard of Yanbei University. The electronic screen outside the lecture hall of the School of Physics was scrolling with red Song fonts - "The First Seminar on the Frontiers of Time Physics". Lin Chen stood in the corridor outside the hall, his fingertips unconsciously rubbing the wear lines on his briefcase. The briefcase contained a paper that he stayed up all night to finalize. Next to the title was a line of small words marked in pencil: "Correction of the mathematical model of nonlinear transitions in time."
"Teacher Lin, are you here too?" A brisk female voice came from behind. Zhou Manqi walked quickly with a stack of bound materials in her arms, with some blue and black ink on the sleeves of her white coat. "I saw your name tag backstage just now, and I was actually scheduled to be the first to speak at the main venue. Are you nervous?"
Lin Chen pulled his tie and smiled. He met Zhou Manqi at last year's quantum mechanics seminar. This girl who had just graduated with a Ph.D. always liked to chase after various experts with her notebook and ask questions. Her eyes were as bright as quenched stars. At this moment, the work card on her chest was not crooked. Lin Chen stretched out his hand to help her straighten it. When the metal buckle touched the fingertips, both of them remembered the embarrassment of knocking over the coffee cup in the tea room last year. At that time, the draft about time paradox in her hand was dislodged by the brown liquid.
The lecture hall gradually filled up with people. Most of the silver-haired old men in the front row were wearing pressed suits, and the conference manuals in their hands were ruffled at the edges; the young scholars in the back row were typing away on their tablets, occasionally looking up at the projection screen above the stage. Lin Chen noticed that there was a man in a dark gray windbreaker sitting in the third row by the window. His profile looked particularly cold in the sunlight. He was spinning a black pen in his hand, but his eyes seemed to be fixed on him.
"Next, I would like to invite Associate Professor Lin Chen from the School of Physics of Yanbei University to give us a report on "Correction of the Mathematical Model of Nonlinear Time Transitions." When the host's voice came through the speaker, Lin Chen felt a thin layer of sweat on his palms. The moment he stepped onto the stage to adjust the microphone, he caught a glimpse of the man in gray trench coat under the stage who suddenly stopped turning his pen and pulled out a palm-sized silver instrument from his briefcase. Light green ripples danced on the screen.
"Traditional time theory believes that the time axis is a linear existence that extends in one direction..." Lin Chen's voice gradually calmed down, and the laser pointer drew bright spots on the curtain. "But according to my derivation in the high-dimensional space equation, when the gravitational field intensity reaches a critical value, time may be partially folded - just like two stacked papers are punctured to form a connected hole."
There was a low discussion in the audience. Zhou Manqi was sitting in the first row. The pen in her hand moved quickly on the notebook. She suddenly raised her head and asked, "Teacher Lin, your model mentioned the 'overlap of time coordinates'. Does this mean that at a certain node, the past and the future will exist at the same time?"
"Theoretically yes." Lin Chen called up a set of three-dimensional coordinate systems. "The key here is to find the resonant frequency of the gravitational field, just like finding the key to open the door."
As soon as he finished speaking, the man in the gray trench coat in the third row suddenly stood up. His voice was low and clear, cutting through the noise in the venue: "Associate Professor Lin, have you considered the irreversibility of this 'jump'? If an object enters the time hole, is it possible for it to return to its original coordinates?"
Lin Chen frowned. This problem hit the weakest link in his model - his derivation could only prove the possibility of time folding, but could not calculate the return trajectory. "There's no perfect solution yet," he admitted, "but I think..."
"I think this is impossible." The man in gray trench coat interrupted him and walked slowly onto the podium. He took out a silver pocket watch from his pocket. The moment he opened the cover, Lin Chen suddenly noticed a light pink scar on his left wrist, shaped like a twisted "s". "Ten years ago, I proposed a similar theory." The man's gaze swept across the audience, "until I saw with my own eyes that the experimental object disintegrated in a strong gravitational field and turned into a string of uncaptured space-time fragments."
There was a sudden silence in the lecture hall. Zhou Manqi opened her eyes wide in surprise, and the pen in her hand fell to the ground with a "clack". Lin Chen stared at the pocket watch. The hands were turning counterclockwise, and a line of vague small words was engraved on the inside of the dial: "19:33, never to return."
"Who are you?" Lin Chen's voice was a little tight.
The man closed his pocket watch, and a complicated smile appeared at the corner of his mouth: "My name is Chen Mo, and I used to be a researcher here." He paused, and his eyes fell on Lin Chen's briefcase, "Teacher Lin, is there a set of correction values for the gravitational constant missing on page 37 of your paper?"
Lin Chen was suddenly stunned. That set of data was an error he discovered late last night before he had time to modify it - how could this man named Chen Mo know?
At this moment, the lights in the lecture hall suddenly flickered. When Zhou Manqi bent down to pick up the pen, she accidentally saw half of the instrument exposed by the hem of Chen Mo's windbreaker. The green ripples on the screen had a strange resonance with the sunlight outside the window. She suddenly remembered the old newspaper she saw in the archives three days ago. In the photo of the laboratory explosion on the front page, there was a blurry figure with a scar like that on his wrist.
"Mr. Chen," Zhou Manqi stood up, her voice trembling imperceptibly, "Did the experiment you mentioned happened in Laboratory No. 3 on September 17, 2013?"
Chen Mo's face turned pale instantly. The pocket watch slipped from his hand and broke in half on the wooden floor of the podium. Countless overlapping shadows were reflected in the glass fragments - there was a young Chen Mo debugging instruments in the laboratory, Lin Chen in a white coat deducing formulas on the blackboard, and a girl with a ponytail squatting on the ground to pick up a pen, exactly like Zhou Manqi at this moment.
The lights went out completely. The moment the emergency lights came on, Lin Chen saw that Chen Mo's figure was becoming transparent, like an ink mark soaked in water. "Stop looking for that set of data," Chen Mo's voice seemed to come from far away, "Some doors can never be closed again..."
When his figure completely disappeared, Lin Chen suddenly found that there was half a broken pocket watch in his hand. The writing on the inside of the dial becomes clearer, and there is a line of newly engraved small characters below: "September 17, 2023, Yanbei University."
The emergency lights go out and normal lighting comes back on. The scholars in the audience were still discussing the debate just now in low voices, as if everything just now was just an illusion. Zhou Manqi picked up the pen on the ground and found a shallow scratch on the cap, which was exactly the same as the pen that fell at the explosion site in the old photo she saw in the archives three days ago.
Lin Chen clenched the half of the pocket watch and suddenly rushed to his seat. He opened his briefcase and took out the thirty-seventh page of the paper - in the originally blank correction column, there was an unknown line of neat handwriting. The handwriting was almost exactly the same as his own: "Correction value of gravitational constant: 6.674184x10^-11, this way is blocked."
The sycamore leaves outside the lecture hall are still falling, and the sun shines through the glass windows and casts moving spots on the floor. Zhou Manqi walked to Lin Chen, looked at the trembling of his fingertips, and suddenly whispered: "Tell me, that person just now...could he come back from ten years later?"
Lin Chen didn't answer. He looked at a sycamore leaf passing by outside the window, and vaguely felt that the trajectory of the leaf seemed to have been seen somewhere before - perhaps in some forgotten formula, perhaps in some upcoming period of time. The gears of the pocket watch were still turning silently, as if they were counting an approaching node.
